CITY OF PASADENA
  City Council Minutes
  May 23, 2022 - 4:30 P.M.

I  City Hall Council Chamber

  The regular meeting was convened and held virtually by videoconference/teleconference.

  OPENING:  Mayor Gordo called the meeting to order at 4:37 p.m. The pledge
  of allegiance was led by Councilmember Rivas.

  ROLL CALL:  Mayor Victor M. Gordo
  Councilmembers:  Vice Mayor Andy Wilson
  Councilmember Tyron Hampton
  Councilmember John J. Kennedy (Absent)
  Councilmember Steve Madison (Arrived at 4:54 p.m.)

  Ceremonial Matters  Mayor Gordo presented a proclamation declaring June 3, 2022 as
  "Gun Violence Awareness Day," in the City Of Pasadena. Lola

I  Osborne, Deputy Director of Parks, Recreation and Community
  Services, accepted the proclamation, and Cindy Montoya, with San
  Gabriel Valley Moms Demand Action, provided information on the
  National Gun Violence Awareness Day, spoke on the need to
  continue to educate the public on the devastating impacts of gun
  violence and invited community members to join the Wear Orange
  Peace Walk on June 4, 2022 honoring Ernesto Ramos Jimenez, as
  Pasadena resident killed by gun violence in 2020.

  In response to Councilmember Hampton's inquiry on an ordinance
  related to illegal ghost guns, and an ordinance on safe storage of
  firearms, Interim City Manager stated that the matter would be
  agendized mid-June or early July.

  Recommendation: : It is recommended that the City Council:

  (3) Direct the City Attorney to prepare an ordinance for the Zoning
  Code Amendment within 60 days consistent with the provisions set

  Recommendation of the Planning Commission: On April 27,
  2022, the Planning Commission considered the proposed Zoning
  Code Amendments at publically noticed hearing, and by a vote of
  7-2, recommended that the City Council approve the proposed
  Zoning Code Amendment as presented by staff, with the following
  recommended amendments:
  1.  Apply Secretary of Interior standards to all sites that are
  historically designated or eligible for designation - no exceptions for
  small projects (included in the staff recommendation);
  2.  Require a 55-year covenant for affordable housing, which will

I  apply even if the religious use vacates the site (staff recommends
  that rental units be subject to an affordability covenant in perpetuity
  and 45-year covenant for ownership units, consistent with the
  inclusionary housing requirements of Section 17.42.070(C). Both
  would remain in effect for the specified timeframe, even if the
  existing religious use vacates the site);
  3.  Clarify that housing developments may occur on sites with
  religious facility use as well as adjacent/contiguous sites also
  owned by the religious institution (included in the staff
  recommendation);
  4.  Clarify the development review process (by right and with
  Design Review) (included in the staff recommendation);
  5.  Clarify that Secretary of Interior standards also apply to
  noncontributing properties within a historic district (included in the
  staff recommendation);
  6.  Prepare a Constitutional Analysis related to allowing housing
  on religious institutional sites, and require that housing projects
  must be developed and operated by an independent nonprofit
  organization (independent from the religious organization) (all
  housing must comply with state and federal laws); and
  7.  Verify that the religious facility is a nonprofit and has owned

I  and operated the site for a minimum of 5 years prior to applying for
  a residential project (included in the staff recommendation).
